writeup.headline: EQT rates Hold at 64, one point short of Buy, as strong margins offset weak trend and growth.
writeup.thesis: EQT scores 64, a Hold that sits just 1 point below the Buy band. Quality is the standout at 95, with an 83.5% gross margin, a 41.8% operating margin, a 40.7% FCF margin and diluted share count up 0.1% year on year. Valuation scores 79: in absolute terms the multiples are fairly low (P/FCF of 9.2x, EV/EBIT of 10.4x, FCF yield 5.8 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield), and against its own history the stock sits near the middle of its own history, with P/FCF cheaper than at 42 of the last 61 month-ends. Holding the score back are growth at 47 (TTM revenue growth of 18.6% but a latest-quarter revenue decline of 9.6% year on year), a balance sheet score of 48 with very little cash against debt, and a trend score of 42 with shares 13.4 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days. News is mildly positive at 56: the pending Range Resources deal would make EQT the largest US gas producer, but analysts trimmed price targets after Q3.
key_risks: Natural gas price swings drove a latest-quarter revenue decline of 9.6% year on year and could hit results again.
Thin cash buffer, with a cash-to-debt ratio of 0.01 and net debt at 1.44 times FCF.
The all-stock Range Resources deal still needs regulatory approval and brings integration and dilution risk.
Weak price trend: shares down 8.0% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and price 17.2% below its 52-week high.
Analysts cut price targets after Q3, which could weigh on sentiment.
what_would_change: A gain of just 1 point would move the rating to Buy, for example from improving relative strength lifting the trend score or a return to quarterly revenue growth lifting the growth score.
A smooth regulatory path for the Range Resources deal or better guidance could raise the news score.
A drop to Sell would need a fall of 20 points, such as a sharp deterioration in margins or valuation alongside weaker prices.
A shrinking FCF yield or rising debt from the acquisition would pressure the valuation and balance sheet scores.
